this is long but bare with me. this place stereotypes people with mental health history. this is strictly for their er doctors and er intake nurses (some). i have past heart problems which were corrected in high school. i was feeling close to the same way the first time i had my heart episode and went to the er in mid november. i went in for heart palpitations, shortness of breath, extreme lethargic about to pass out feeling, and weakness. when i was taken to the er by my boyfriend, because who wants to call an ambulance on their lunch break in their work parking garage and drawl that kind of attention to themselves, when i got there, the intake nurses literally did not fucking care i existed as a human. it took the nurses or security guards who help wheel people in and out to tell them to open the door and let me in. the er intake nurse didn't give rats a$$ that i couldn't breath well, didn't pay attention to my boyfriend who was literally handing her an emergency card i keep in my wallet of all my allergies and medical history. my boyfriend told them my symptoms, they didn't even think about hooking me up to a ekg until i was in the er exam room, which if i can remember correctly was about 15 to 20 minutes after i arrived. the nurses were ok that day and the nurse who put my iv in kept moving it because she couldn't get the blood out...ok we'll go somewhere else?! so much pain while feeling like i could pass out. 

next the doctor comes in. talks about my symptoms, some history, so on. the moment i mentioned i was on an anti depressant with past history of anxiety, it switched his questions. it went from asking about how i was feeling physically to asking me if i was stressed, or sad, or anxious...so on with the other related questions. look, doc, i know the difference between heart problems and an anxiety attack, this is not an anxiety attack. so instead of ordering more tests he gives me an anti anxiety med, and let's me chill out for an hour or so. of course a anxiety med like xanax is going to chill me out and slow down my heart and breathing. been on them before in high school and anyone who has a friend in their residency at a top tier hospital can tell you, "yea that med is going to make your heart slow down and relax any symptoms." never once consulted a on staff cardiologist or offering to wait to have one come down because of my past history. given my previous heart problem, if anyone remotely understands the heart knows that things can come back and not in the same way as before!!! after this i was discharged and told if i have any more symptoms to come back. 

the next day and a half i slept, no joke, 18 hours out of a 24 hour day. i could still feel heart beats skip, still had shortness of breath just doing small things like going up stairs or even getting up to go to the bathroom. i didn't want to eat or even talk. so after a day and a half of not feeling like a functioning person, i went back.

this time the intake nurses took me seriously, hooked me up to ekg right away, and got an iv in me right away. this doctor took me seriously and ordered a ct with contrast to check for blood clots and did a few blood pressure tests based on laying and standing. everything came back normal. the moment i knew she looked at the most recent visit, started the, "are you sure you're not anxious," questions came out. in my head i'm thinking, "are you flipping kidding me?! does no one take me seriously?!" the one thing i will never forget the doctor saying to me is, " if you are feeling bad and don't get answers the first time, you shouldn't come back to the er. go see the doctors we referred you to the first time." i'm sorry what!????! i was literally doing what the discharge papers said. it's not my problem ( well kinda is if i die from not well examined heart issue) if you didn't exhaust all your resources to help or passed me along because you gave up. i started to cry. the only person who gave me hope was the nurse. she literally ask me, "do you feel safe to go home?" i flat out started crying, and said no. and told her i would never return here for any emergency. i told her i rather drive to a further hospital and die on the way, than come to this hospital again. she took that seriously and comforted me. i was discharged sent home waiting to see a cardiologist 2 weeks later. 

that cardiologist was pissed no one consulted a cardiologist on staff. i got an eco, heart monitor for a week, and a stress test, i have a problem with my sinus node and will need to have surgery. something that could have been solved and found in that moment if someone didn't profile me as a depressed anxious person!!! 

seriously, tell your doctors to stop stereotyping people with mental health problems. stop thinking that someone with a valid history of cardiac problems and a mental health past is just making it up and is just "anxious."

my husband has been a patient at mj several times. the first time, mj was an independent facility. therapists and nursing staff were both wonderful; efficient, well-trained and competent, very caring, and seemingly happy in their positions. in 2018 northwestern bought the facility. the facility has become very "corporate." while the therapy is still top-notch, the staff has taken on a different attitude toward their patients and their jobs. they are no longer caring and friendly; those traits enhance the patient and family experience and speed the healing process - lack of those traits make the patient want to get out of there before they are actually ready. the nursing staff, particularly the night shift, are "businesslike" to the point of being rude. the medical staff is also poor, at best, in communicating with patients and family and seem incompetent in following the discharge orders of the hospital from which the patient came, even to the point of simply ignoring the medication orders without informing the ordering physician or the patient/family. 
i am so disappointed that a superior facility like marianjoy would "sell out" to the corporate world which is taking over so much of medicine today. i would still return to mj strictly for the therapy, but i am certainly not happy about the new atmosphere and i honestly don't know if i would blanketly recommend the facility as i once did. 
i find that outpatient therapy at a dupage medical group facility is as good if the patient is capable of doing op therapy.
of course, there are still several staff members who maintain the old fashioned bedside manner and at least try to go above and beyond in patient care, but even those seem to be "afraid of breaking corporate protocol."

i want to write a review on the inpatient dining "expressly for you." there is a menu that you can order what you want. there are specific times that you must be followed in ensure your meal order is placed in time. i have ordered many things from the menu, overall, i think they try to be to fancy and offer too many complex meal options. when i am sick, i prefer to eat very simple things without a ton of spice or flavor. this may just be me, but here are some of my thoughts on things i have ordered. 

scrambled eggs: the first time i ordered scrambled eggs they arrived with onions and peppers. this was not expected. the next time i ordered, i specified that i wanted scrambled eggs plain without onions or peppers. this time it arrived with a garnish orange slice that spread orange juice on my eggs and rendering them inedible. if you just want eggs, order without garnish! 

oatmeal: this is a solid basic. it is pretty bland by itself, but would highly recommend adding banana slices and a packet of cream cheese. 

pimento cheese plate: this is a generous scoop of pimento cheese and served with fresh veggies and pita. i wasn't feeling up to eating much, but what i did eat was great! 

cheeseburger and fries: one night i didn't get a dinner order placed, so they brought me a late tray option. it was a freshly made burger and fries. i may have just been super hungry, but this was amazing!! 

chicken salad sandwich: this was okay. the chicken salad had too much mayo for my taste, but not bad. 

chicken tenders: there was a lot of breading, but easy to peel off.

baked potato: good simple option and can order shredded cheese and sour cream on the side.

clear liquid diet: i'm not sure much can be done to make this better, but this is rough! the tray comes with broth (i sampled vegetable, chicken, and beef), jello, juice, or flavored water. the broth was always luke warm and never appealing, but this is likely a result of how i was feeling. pro tip:  the floors stock popsicles, so that is a great alternative/supplement to the tray. 

if you miss ordering off the menu or get to your room late the floors stock some boxed meals. one night my diet was advanced from clears to regular diet late and i wanted solid food. they brought me a turkey sandwich boxed lunch. i ate the turkey (not then bread) a standard basic turkey sandwich which is a good option when the cafeteria is closed. 

things i wish were on the menu: greek yogurt. they have sugary yogurt, but i really wish there was greek yogurt, low fat string cheese sticks, plain tuna without being in tuna salad, or other high protein simple options. 

the people that take your order on the phone are really helpful and willing to get you want you want!

the main reason for this post is that the er staff mishandled information that caused them to break hipaa and i now have the personal information of a previous patient of this hospital. i do not believe this was intentional, but was a very careless mistake. there were several instances where this could have been caught prior to myself noticing it at the end of our visit. 

on tuesday morning 2/18 my boyfriend was not well and asked to be taken to the er and we went to broward hospital imperial point. due to his level of pain he was distracted and asked if i could handle the signing in and provided at check in with his driver's license and completed the intake form. 

after maybe 10 minutes the nurses came in to set my boyfriend up with an iv drip, etc. we were seen by the er doctor/pa (john marini), who came in to talk to my boyfriend who was in a lot of pain so i was assisting with some of the questions. due to where the pain was located the doctor ordered for an ultrasound of his abdomen and morphine for the pain. 

question #1: why are basic questions not being asked prior to ordering expensive tests? it is the middle of flu season and patient comes in with abdominal pain after vomiting for 5 hours. no pain over mcburney's point. at no time during the entire visit did anyone ask about if he had the flu shot, would he like a flu shot, or do any kind of test swabs for the flue.  immediately they went for more expensive tests. 

the er doctor/pa came to discuss that it looked like from the ultrasound that something with his gallbladder and pancreas, and that he wanted to order a ct scan. at this time another girl, administrative, rolled in a cart with a computer and began to go over basic patient information, much of what i had literally just filled out on the intake form or could be found on his license. doctor/pa was still present, as well as another nurse. 

the girl went through the list - name, birthday, address, emergency contact, etc. none of the information that they had on file was what i had filled out and we didn't recognize anything...

question #2: is it not protocol to ask the patients for their birthday and then the patient provides it? this girl was literally reading off what was on file, and each item we had no idea where that information was coming from. they had the wrong address, wrong birthday, we had never heard of the person that was the emergency contact. at no point during this initial confirmation of information did anyone ask him for his ssn, or i'm sure this would have been caught immediately. 

they took my boyfriend for a ct and he eventually returned. the doctor/pa returned to let us know that it didn't show any issues, that his gallbladder was contracted and nothing wrong with his pancreas (not shocking, ordered an expensive test for nothing without checking off all of the other things that it could be first). he would get us set up to be discharged. he also made some kind of comment that my boyfriend had been to the er back in 2015, which my boyfriend has never been there. 

while we continued to wait and i was holding my boyfriend's hand, at that point i noticed that the birthday on his wristband was incorrect. and that was when it clicked in my head that they 100% had some other patient's information and did not have the right patient. 

i went up to the girl who had been confirming all the information before and told her "the birthday on his wristband is wrong. when we were going over information before, we didn't know the emergency contact, you had the wrong address and phone number, are you sure  you have the right person?". she looked concerned and rolled her computer back in. now, finally, one of the first questions that she asked was for him to confirm the last 4 digits of his ssn. when he did, her eyes got wide with an 'oh s***' kind of look. so i directly asked her "is what i think is happening actually happening?" and she quietly said that she thought that i was right. i asked if that changed anything that had just happened here today, and she said "it doesn't change anything for you guys but it changes a lot for me" and rolled her little cart out. i have no idea if she fixed it or if she reported it.

after all of that, somehow the prescriptions and the documents that have personal information written on them still have the wrong birthday, wrong phone number wrong address. they are someone else's, whoever was there in 2015 apparently. searching the address on google i find that it was associated with someone who has the same first and last name as my boyfriend (different middle initial) and the name of the person that they had originally told us was his listed emergency contact. i can literally google map image their home. i could call this person's phone number if i wanted to because i have it due to the hospital's mistakes.

when the weights did not work she asked me if i wanted her to try again to force my arm in the joint.  i told her again i want an ortho doctor.  she said after weights the next step is to put me under in the trauma room.  i said what makes you think you can to it when i'm asleep, if you can't do it when i'm awake.  she said my arm will be easier to manipulate.  i again told her to try.  another male resident was pushing on the back of my shoulder as hard as he could.  his hard pushing would have hurt if he did that on any part of my body.  meanwhile, she was twisting my arm trying to get it in the socket.  the uci ladies (two) that would alternate sitting in the room across from my room (watching the patient in that room) kept turning their chairs around so they could watch.  they stared as if watching tv.  it was so rude! ! the doctors - resident, attending, rn, never thought to close my door a little so i could have privacy. 
after pushing/pulling, weights, pushing/pulling, she said we now should put you under. i again told her i want an ortho doctor and that an ortho doctor could have resolved this a long time ago.  she again told me she could do this. she said she was having such a hard time getting my shoulder back in because i waited so long to come in (i came in 5 hours after the fall).  this is a typical response from a woman that cannot get the job done and so blame their lack of expertise on the patient.  while waiting for a trauma room i asked the rn about getting an ortho doctor.  he said he did call-out.  dr matonis never told me that.  the trauma room was finally available.  it did not look to me like anyone was in any of the trauma rooms to begin with.  she told the tech to put a mask on me, but he told her is was not needed, since i had the nose tube. she then told others in the room that they will learn a lot when the ortho doctor comes.  after it was over the tech told me ortho, dr choi, was there and assisted.  dr matonis never told me anything.  never saw her after.  they wrapped  shoulder stabilizer around my bra under my clothes.  my belly showed. no one helped.  now x-rays show a possible fracture which did not show in 1st set.

doc_text:
where do i begin.  this has taken place during the covid-19 lock down-no family, no visitors. i had to rely on the nursing staff to keep me abreast of my 85-year-old sisters condition. you can only hope that you and your loved one are never put in this hideous, stressful situation! although, my sister was walking when admitted, a few days later she could not walk and her speech didn't sound right, kind of slurred. (could not get out of bed). i requested a phone call from the doctor, but never got one.

i discovered that she was put on the covid-19 floor even though she did not have the virus. i was told that everyone goes to that unit until their test comes back negative twice. then they are moved to another floor.

the day after she was admitted i called her and there was an ear piercing alarm going off in her room. her door was shut and the call button was not within her reach. she was in tears because this noise was nonstop for who knows how long and it was ear deafening! she said it goes off in the middle of the night when she is sleeping and wakes her.  i immediately hung up and called the nurses station. when the nurse picked up her phone i told her the situation and she literally laughed! oh yes, she said, when you have an intravenous tube in your arm that alarm goes off if you bend your elbow. i was in disbelief! how could you subject an 85 year old to this who can't get out of bed and can't reach her call button and you have her door closed?

also, her phone was put in a place where she could not reach it when i called. this happened more than once! trying to get someone at the nurses desk/station to help with this situation was a horrendous experience!!! if they answer the phone they might transfer you to your loved ones nurse who might answer their phone, but might not.

 one day i called the nurses desk for the second time because i couldn't reach my sister, and the nurse that picked up could hear me fine until i asked to speak to my sisters nurse.  she then did the "hello? hello? hello? i can't hear you" act and then hung up on me.  her name is bethany on the third floor.  she could hear me fine! 

 two days later, after putting in 8 phone calls in over a half hour, i finally got my sisters nurse, who had to check first to see if she was his patient, although i was told later that he had seen her that morning. i told him what i had been through and how frustrated i was at that point so he than told me he would walk in there with his phone so i could talk to her, but once again the phone hung up before that happened. my 9th phone call, the operator told me she would connect me to the floor supervisor who assured me he would make sure that my sisters nurse would call me right back.

he called and told me he was with my sister but that he was having a hard time waking her. she would open her eyes but than close them immediately. he said "i don't know if this is her base line."
i couldn't believe my ears. no, i said this is not her baseline! he didn't know her baseline? he had not been informed when he came on shift of the condition of his patients? she is like you or i, very alert, talking and awake during the day. there's something wrong with her! i don't know how long she was in this state. 

turns out they thought she had a stroke! they hadn't even noticed! thank goodness i insisted the nurse go in and check on her! later the neurologist called who hadn't even examined my sister, this was on may 26th, and told me the report said she had fainted. when i questioned this, in a smart ass way her reply was "were you there? because the last time i checked relatives and visitors are not allowed in the hospital because of covid-19." (i wish i could remember her name.) yes, i was there, on the phone, and she did not faint! 

they claimed it was a sudden change, that she was awake and talking that morning. so i ask why did the nurse not know that comatose was not her baseline then.? it just doesn't add up.

my sister is still there and today she was not answering her phone again. when i called the nurses station for room 428 the nurse that picked up told me that "her board did not show that anyone was in that room". what????????? she has been in that room now for 2 days.  i hung up and called the hospital operator who assured me that my sister was in room 428 and asked if i would like to be connected with her nurses cell phone. thank goodness for the operators at fawcett memorial hospital. they were the only ones that were truly helpful. if it weren't for them i would have gone out of my mind!

we still haven't gotten to the bottom of what actually happened to my sister and we probably will never know. there's more, but i've already written a book! im praying my sister will be released from there tomorrow.

needless to say, we are done with fawcett memorial hospital!

my mom has been battling cancer for the last 3 years and recently got pneumonia. her cancer drs are at cedars and coh (city of hope). unfortunately the ambalance brought her to the closest hospital so. this hospital is not equipped to deal with cancer patients/serious illnesses. after a week of my mom being in the hospital, she ended up in icu. 

the case managers are horrible! we needed my mom transferred to cedars. you need an accepting dr from the other hospital which we had but they had no beds. i dealt with daisy and eric and their compassion level is zero. most people might say things like i'm sorry for what you're going through, i can't imagine how hard this might be, or we are trying our best. any empathy would have been nice during this stressful time. i knew cedars or coh would be able to treat my mom better so i was trying to move her asap.    

also coh had a bed but soh never offered me one. it's really hard to get into another hospital so when a bed opened up they should have told me! i had to hire a patient advocate to get my mom to the coh even though they had a bed available a week before. the timing was crucial in getting my mom to the coh. also the drs couldn't decide if my mom had pneumonia or pneumonitis. the cat scan should've have confirmed this.                

once we got to the coh they told me she had both pneumonia and pneumonitis. also, they immediately did a bronchoscopy which soh never did. this was the only way to save my mom's life. it was really important to see what was growing in her lungs. like the 2 fungus, virus and bacterial infection so they know how to treat her. at soh it was nice dr. stacey gave me his cell # to address my concerns but why couldn't they figure out my mom had 5 infections. 

my friend asked soh if my mom could have an infection called c-diff because my mom was having continuous diarrhea. they told me they thought it was the ensures. the nurses couldn't even figure out my mom had one of the most common infections from all the anabiotic's. my friend who is a nurse had to tell them to test for it!  

cdiff it's highly contagious and puts us at risk for getting this infection. you're supposed to wear gloves, a gown, and a mask anytime you enter the room. we had been doing none of this.  

the worst thing about this hospital is some of the nurses. tonya in icu is not only rude but she's completely incompetent. i called and my mom's heartbeat was a fib with a heart rate of 171! your heart beat should be 60-100. they told me they were transferring her out of icu. i forced them to call a dr and he ordered medicine immediately and to stay in icu! also they had a device up her nose to monitor her continuous fever. when i called they told me my mom didn't have a fever. when i walked in her monitor said 96.1 but my mom felt super hot. she also had complained to her nurse lyn she was hot. any moron could've figured out my mom had a fever. we took her temperature by mouth and it was 104.5! i immediately called for a charge nurse. it took us hours to get her fever down. we needed a cooling blanket and a ice bath to bring the fever down. also my mom had diarrhea all over her. when i asked her nurse when is the last time she had been changed she said early that morning!

after my mom kept having diarrhea they put an anal probe in so it would catch all the diarrhea. they insisted this was necessary. once we got to coh they said those probes cause anal bleeding and should never be used. the nurses are just  lazy and don't want to do their job even if my mom has discomfort or risk an infection.   

for some reason at soh my mom had a continuous fever but the day she got to coh no fevers. i'm not quite sure what they were doing to her at so but i do know that they weren't conducting the proper treatments needed. keep in mind this is the icu, the best care she could have gotten! my mom arrived to coh not in icu and her level of care went up 10x. she has a respiratory therapist w/ 4 breathing treatments a day. someone to bathe her so she's clean at all times. a team to avoid bedsores/rashes. (in soh my mom had a starting bedsore and a rash from them not cleaning her butt)  

the day we came into coh she got her bronchoscopy, which they did not do at so. if they did they would've found out that she had a very serious life-threatening fungal infection that needs to be treated as early as possible. it grows very fast so if it's not caught early you can die. the only good thing about soh is the nurses (renee/allen/charles) which are not complete idiots like the rest of the hospital. 

i'm not writing a bad review because i'm angry my mom could die. i'm writing to warn others that this hospital really is bad. there's a reason why there are no beds at cedars or the coh. they don't have the experience or technology to treat illnesses and infections. the best advice i can give you is if you dont want them to kill your family member don't come here!

i agree with both reviews of janny k and tina k. i am giving one star for there were times, not many, that i could speak into my father's ear over the phone- briefly. my father passed away due to their negligence!! families need to be with their loved one's during recovering; 1 for advocacy and the other for support and love!! my father, prior to being transferred here from icu, was alert and fully cognizant.  he just needed long term recovery for he still required a ventilator and had a trach and g-tube. please keep in mind that this occurred during the covid-19 epidemic, therefore, visitation was not allowed. this was very difficult for us and the only updates that we could get were via telephone. as far as zoom/face time, the client advocate informed me that unfortunately we could only see my father 2x per week via zoom for only 10 to 15min. there was not enough man power to see your loved one daily.  this was not so pleasing to our ear but 2x was better then none. i unfortunately never got to see my father for our face time appointment; he passed away prior to the first scheduled zoom meeting. 
the first morning and afternoon of admittance, everything seemed normal as far as updates. however, the first alarming news was when i spoke to the case manager who stated that my father was not responding. my father was responding and following commands/nodding yes or no to questions prior to the transfer.  also, the case manager stated that he had an occupational therapy evaluation and that he was not following simple commands. this was also alarming, for prior to that day he was receiving physical therapy at icu and following commands. the day shift nurse that day did me the favor of placing me in my father's ear via telephone so that he can hear my voice. however, the night shift nurse stated that they were too busy. this particular nurse mentioned that he had 9 patients during his shift; 9 patients? how can one nurse be in charge of 9 patients? are patients being constantly moved and cleaned?  every time i would call to speak to someone, it seemed as though they were overwhelm or too busy. we received contradicting information as well. the following day, i inquired about the medication/antibiotics that my father was receiving and the day shift nurse stated that he was not receiving any- what? he had pneumonia- why was he not receiving the antibiotics that were administered to him? she stated that my father's white blood counts were okay and he was fighting a fever therefore he did not have an infection- what?? if your body has a fever, your body is fighting an infection! she informed me that my father was only being administered tylenol for the fever. i called the house supervisor immediately and asked to speak to the doctor in charge. the house supervisor seemed overwhelmed as well when i spoke to her. she indicated that if she had time, she would do her best to call the doctor and inform him. i never spoke with the doctor. i called the number that they provided and never heard from him. i called the night shift nurse that day and he stated that he was receiving antibiotics. i asked, " which one is it- either he is receiving or not"? what was there plan of care for my father?  the following day my father passed away. we live about 86 miles away from baldwin park, therefore when we arrived, my father was already deceased. the doctor was not present when we arrived and we demanded for him to come back and speak to us as to what occurred. the doctor did finally return and sat with my family and i, alongside with the head nurse and house supervisor. the  doctor used the term "supposedly" my father threw up and they stopped administering food to him. " supposedly"- what really occurred? the doctor looked at the staff nurse and supervisor when informing us of the incident-as though trying to make sure that they were on the same page. 
conclusion- my father did not receive the proper care that he needed here. he needed constant care for his vent settings as well as for his trach and g-tube. when we walked in to see my father's body, the staff kept to themselves as though scared to speak to us. as we walked the hallways, many of the patients looked as though they were already near death. i deeply regret sending my father here. the room in which my father was in, was not what we expected. there was no chart on the walls explaining who was the nurse, etc. the family pictures, that we asked the nurses to place on his wall, were not displayed. they were tucked away/shoved away in the closet. the room, although shared with two other patients, felt lonely. my brother mentioned as he was mourning my father's dead body that day( they only allowed two family members at a time), that a staff member walked in to ask," where are they taking his body." seriously- we just received the news that my father passed and you see us mourning his body- no empathy here ! please do not send your loved one here!
